articles.title: Wigan Warriors 6-33 Wakefield Trinity: Daryl Powell's side through to Super League Grand Final after producing major upset
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity produced one of the biggest upsets in the history of the Super League play-offs as they sealed a huge 33-6 victory against Wigan Warriors to advance to their first-ever Grand Final.
articles.body:
Wakefield Trinity booked their place in their first-ever Super League Grand Final on Saturday night as they produced a huge upset to defeat Wigan Warriors 33-6; watch Warrington vs Wakefield in the Super League Grand Final live on Sky Sports Main Event

Wakefield Trinity produced one of the biggest upsets in the history of the Super League play-offs as they sealed a huge 33-6 victory against Wigan Warriors to advance to their first-ever Grand Final.

League Leaders Shield winners Wigan had not lost in their last 16 games across all competitions, and were hot favourites to advance to their third-straight Super League Grand Final, but they were left stunned by a ferocious Wakefield team, who, had been playing their rugby in the Championship two years ago.

After a cagey first half, the visitors capitalised on what would be a costly second-half sin bin for Warriors playmaker Adam Keighan, running in a trio of tries from Tom Johnstone, Jack Sinfield and Corey Hall inside seven minutes as they romped their way to a 27-point victory.

"I thought we were superb," Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell said. "We completed at 100 per cent in the second half, 94 per cent in the first half. We made one error all game.

"Wigan are excellent, and they've had an unbelievable season, but I thought we were unbelievable tonight. We started a little bit shaky but once we got our teeth into the game

"It's a special group of boys and we've got an amazing opportunity next week now."

The first half was a cagey affair, with both sides matching each other's intensity, but it would be Wigan who would take the advantage first after Trinity's Jazz Tevaga was sent to the sin bin for a trip on Liam Marshall.

Brad O'Neill made the visitors pay, bulldozing his way over, but Wakefield hit back through Johnstone, who finished off a superb move in the corner.

Wigan lacked discipline at times, and a penalty right in front of the posts for a ruck infringement saw Trinity take a two-point advantage heading into the break.

The second half continued with the same intensity, with neither side able to pull away.

But a tip-tackle from Keighran on Isaiah Vagana proved a decisive moment, with the Warriors five-eighth being shown a yellow card.

Wakefield immediately attacked, with Johnstone capitalising on a mismatched defence, crossing over in the corner with another sensational finish, before Sinfield bulldozed his way past Junior Nsemba for another try moments later.

Powell's side had a third within seven minutes of Keighran's sin bin, with Hall flying down the wing before crossing the finish line.

Jake Trueman was brilliant throughout the match, and popped off a lovely offload to Ky Rodwell, who crashed over for the final try of the match.

"They had to be very good to punish us when we lost Adam [Keighran]," Wigan Warriors head coach Matty Peet said on Keighran's sin bin.

"No way is this game about that. We were well beaten. Wakefield deserve it. We were well prepared, we were motivated but they were too good.

"I can see why it was given, there's always opinions, but this game's not about that."

"Credit to Wakefield, it hurts, but the night belongs to them."

articles.summary: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Noruega y Portugal en el Ullevaal Stadium correspondiente a la jornada 2 del Grupo 4 de la Liga A de la Nations League
articles.body: Noruega afronta su segundo compromiso en esta Nations League después de sacar adelante un estreno complicado frente a Dinamarca. El conjunto nórdico consiguió imponerse gracias a un doblete de Erling Haaland, que volvió a demostrar su capacidad para marcar diferencias en un partido de máxima exigencia y sigue engrosando sus cifras a nivel de selección. Ahora, los noruegos tratarán de repetir resultado ante su afición en un duelo ante otra de las grandes selecciones europeas. Favorito para el partido entre Noruega y Portugal Portugal, por su parte, también comenzó con victoria su andadura en esta edición de la Nations League, donde defiende título. El combinado luso se impuso a Gales por la mínima gracias a un solitario gol de Joao Félix en un encuentro en el que, además, consiguió mantener su portería a cero. El duelo se presenta muy equilibrado para las casas de apuestas: Betfair ofrece una cuota de 2.40 por la victoria de Noruega, 3.50 por el empate y 2.70 por el triunfo de Portugal. Ambos equipos marcan El mercado de ambos equipos marcan aparece como una opción destacada en las apuestas deportivas. Especialmente, teniendo en cuenta los resultados de ambos conjuntos en su estreno. Noruega cumplió este pronóstico ante Dinamarca en un partido en el que consiguió marcar dos goles... pero también encajó. Portugal, en cambio, no lo hizo frente a Gales, ya que Joao Félix fue el único goleador del encuentro y Diogo Costa consiguió mantener su portería a cero. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 1.40 por el 'sí' y de 2.80 por el 'no'. Primer equipo en marcar El mercado del primer equipo en marcar presenta una tendencia similar en los dos combinados, ya que tanto Noruega como Portugal fueron capaces de adelantarse en el marcador durante sus respectivos estrenos en la Nations League. Los noruegos tomaron la iniciativa ante Dinamarca gracias al tanto de Bobb, mientras que Portugal también encontró primero el camino del gol frente a Gales gracias a Joao Félix. Betfair paga a 1.83 que Noruega sea el primer equipo en marcar y a 1.91 que lo haga Portugal. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La línea de goles muestra, en cambio, una dinámica diferente entre los dos encuentros de la primera jornada. En el duelo entre Noruega y Dinamarca se superaron los 2.5 goles totales, con un marcador que terminó reflejando la capacidad ofensiva de ambos combinados. En el caso de Portugal y Gales, esta barrera no se alcanzó, ya que el solitario tanto de Joao Félix decidió el encuentro. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 1.45 por que se superen los 2.5 goles y de 2.55 por que se registren menos de 2.5 tantos.

articles.title: Ian Poveda enfrenta graves cargos en Inglaterra, acusado de fraude y obstrucción a la justicia
articles.standfirst: Nuevo escándalo en Atlético Nacional: Poveda, acusado de irregularidades de tránsito y falsedad documental en su paso por el fútbol inglés
articles.summary: Nuevo escándalo en Atlético Nacional: Poveda, acusado de irregularidades de tránsito y falsedad documental en su paso por el fútbol inglés
articles.body: El futbolista Ian Poveda, atacante de Atlético Nacional, afronta un lío judicial en Inglaterra tras ser acusado formalmente de seis cargos que incluyen obstrucción a la justicia y fraude. La situación jurídica del jugador anglocolombiano se dio a conocer luego de su comparecencia virtual ante un tribunal británico, en vísperas de un importante compromiso de la Liga BetPlay. El pasado 23 de septiembre de 2026, Poveda se presentó mediante videoconferencia ante el juez Robin Mairs en el Centro Judicial Combinado de Leeds. Durante la audiencia, el futbolista de 26 años se declaró inocente de todos los cargos imputados por la Policía de West Yorkshire. En la misma causa penal están vinculados otros dos ciudadanos ingleses: Adekunle Adeyemi (36 años) y Anthony Howe (63 años), quienes también se declararon no culpables. El proceso en contra de Poveda se enfoca en irregularidades de tránsito y falsedad documental presuntamente cometidas durante su paso por el fútbol inglés: pesar de la apertura formal del proceso, el juez fijó el inicio del juicio para diciembre de 2028, por lo que el jugador mantendrá su presunción de inocencia mientras avanza el trámite legal en el Reino Unido y continúa su participación deportiva con Atlético Nacional.

articles.title: Asian Games: Tajinderpal Singh Toor misses hat-trick of golds, wins silver in shot put
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Tajinderpal Singh Toor’s bid for a historic hat-trick of Asian Games gold medals ended with a silver on Saturday as the defending champion
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Tajinderpal Singh Toor’s bid for a historic hat-trick of Asian Games gold medals ended with a silver on Saturday as the defending champion finished second in the men’s shot put at Aichi-Nagoya.Toor, who won gold at the 2018 Jakarta and 2022 Hangzhou Games, produced a best throw of 20.64m to claim his third successive Asian Games medal. However, he could not complete a hat-trick of gold medals after Iran’s Mohammadreza Tayebise produced a Games-record throw of 20.81m to take the top prize.Tayebise’s winning effort also erased Toor’s previous Games record of 20.75m, set when he won gold in Jakarta in 2018.Saudi Arabia’s Mohammed Tolu completed the podium with a throw of 20.48m to win bronze.Asian Games Full Coverage | Medal Tally | ScheduleToor adds another medal to Asian Games collectionAlthough Toor missed out on a third consecutive gold, the silver continued his remarkable consistency at the continental showpiece. He had entered the competition as the two-time defending champion and one of India’s established athletics medal hopes.The 31-year-old’s 20.64m effort was not enough to match Tayebise, who raised the Games record by 6cm.Toor’s silver also added another medal to India’s growing haul in Aichi-Nagoya.Two Indian sprinters reach 200m finalIndia also kept its medal hopes alive in the women’s sprint events. Harita Bhadra and Unnathi Bolland both qualified for Sunday’s 200m final.Bhadra clocked 23.31 seconds to finish second in her heat and secure automatic qualification, while Bolland advanced after finishing third in her heat in 23.33 seconds.In the 100m hurdles, Nandhini Kongan reached the final after finishing fourth in her heat in 13.48 seconds. articles.title: ‘Trying to pull out’: Tyson Fury erupts as Anthony Joshua fight thrown into major doubt just hours after official confirmation
articles.summary: Tyson Fury has thrown the highly anticipated fight against Anthony Joshua into jeopardy just hours after it was announced, citing disputes involving promoters and accusing Joshua and Hearn of attempting to withdraw from the match. This article explores the unfolding tensions, contractual issues, and potential replacements for the bout scheduled for December 11.
articles.body: Tyson Fury's long-awaited fight with Anthony Joshua has been officially announced for December, but within hours of the confirmation, Fury was already warning that the biggest all-British heavyweight fight in years could be in trouble. The bout is scheduled for December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium and will be broadcast on Netflix, yet a dispute between Joshua's promoter Eddie Hearn and UFC president Dana White has suddenly put the agreement under pressure.Fury turns on Joshua and Hearn after fight announcementFury's warning came after Hearn publicly objected to White's involvement in the promotion of the fight, despite the event being announced as a collaboration between Saudi boxing powerbroker Turki Alalshikh's The Ring and White's UFC operation.Speaking to IFL TV, Hearn said White's involvement was not acceptable under the terms of the agreement surrounding the fight.“Dana White cannot be involved with this fight promotion. Netflix clearly didn't get the memo. No-one talks to each other,” Hearn said.Fury responded on Instagram by accusing Joshua and Hearn of trying to withdraw from the fight, with the former heavyweight champion directing most of his anger towards Hearn.“Anthony Joshua and Eddie Hearn are trying to pull out of this fight. They're saying they're not going to fight now,” Fury said.“It's mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego. He's making up a million different things and threatening we're not going to fight.”Fury then launched into a much more colourful attack, calling Joshua and Hearn “little s***house cowards” and telling Joshua to “pull your finger out” before describing him as a “white-flagged, yellow belly coward”.The former champion also mocked Joshua as a “bodybuilding sausage” and a “little nugget”, while accusing Hearn of allowing personal grievances to threaten the fight.“Now you've got Turki Al-Sheikh finding alternative real men who will fight at the drop of a hat,” Fury said. “So I hope you are happy, you little cowardly b***s. I've never seen anything like you, you pure shouses.”Fury finished the post by directing another insult at Hearn and claiming his promoter dispute had cost boxing its biggest fight.“And this is mainly to do with Eddie Hearn's ego, what a little p****. It's cost us the biggest fight in boxing history. Clown.”The situation is particularly striking because the fight had only just been formally announced, after years of negotiations between the two heavyweight camps repeatedly collapsing.Why Dana White has become the latest obstacleThe disagreement centres on White, who has been publicly feuding with Hearn since the launch of Zuffa Boxing earlier this year.Reports have suggested that White wanted a significant role in promoting the Fury-Joshua event and had hoped the fight would take place in the United States. Hearn, meanwhile, worked to secure the Principality Stadium in Cardiff, where the fight is now scheduled to take place.The contractual position has become central to the dispute, with reports indicating that the agreement requires the fight to take place in the United Kingdom and that White must not be involved in its promotion.White appeared to play into the speculation after Fury's comments, posting a photograph of himself on a video call with Alalshikh while smoking a cigar.Fury subsequently posted another video in which he again blamed Hearn's objections to White for putting the event at risk.“So Eddie Hearn's ego is trying to cost us and all the boxing fans around the world the fight that everyone's waited for, for over a decade,” Fury said.“And it is all because Eddie doesn't want someone in the building. Isn't that a bit pathetic and childish?”Fury then continued his attack on Hearn, accusing him of acting like a child because of his dislike of White.“You absolute nugget. You little silver-spooned wer. You're not a man of your word, you little back-out py.”He also turned his attention back towards Joshua, saying: “And Joshua, you ought to be ashamed of yourself. You want this and you want that.”Hearn's comments and Fury's response have therefore created another major complication for a fight that has already survived several rounds of failed negotiations. Neither side has publicly confirmed that the bout has been cancelled, but the dispute has raised a genuine question over whether the December date can hold.Fury-Joshua has already survived years of failed negotiationsThe latest dispute is only the newest chapter in a fight that has repeatedly appeared close to happening before falling apart.In 2020, the two camps agreed the basis of a two-fight deal, creating the first serious framework for Fury and Joshua to meet.A year later, contracts were signed for an undisputed heavyweight contest, but Deontay Wilder's successful arbitration case forced Fury into a third fight with the American instead.The negotiations returned in 2022, when Joshua accepted a 60-40 split to challenge Fury, but that attempt also collapsed without the fight being made.Fury and Joshua finally signed contracts for their long-awaited meeting earlier this year, with the date and venue formally confirmed this week.Ring Magazine's Mike Coppinger reported that replacement fights were already being worked on because of concerns surrounding White's role in the event. According to Coppinger, unbeaten cruiserweight champion David Benavidez is being considered as a potential replacement opponent for Fury if Joshua pulls out.If the Fury-Joshua fight were to collapse altogether, another alternative involving Ryan Garcia and Terence Crawford has also been discussed, although Crawford retired last year.For now, Fury and Joshua remain scheduled to meet on December 11 at Cardiff's Principality Stadium, with Netflix set to broadcast the fight. articles.title: La arquera que jugó en Colombia y debuta en OnlyFans desata ola de reacciones
articles.standfirst: Lola Gallardo, la portera española que abrió cuenta en OnlyFans
articles.summary: Lola Gallardo, la portera española que abrió cuenta en OnlyFans
articles.body: La guardameta y capitana del Atlético de Madrid Femenino, Lola Gallardo, se convirtió en el centro de la atención mediática y deportiva tras anunciar su incorporación a la plataforma de suscripción OnlyFans. La arquera que jugó en Colombia en contra Atlétco Huila en Techo en 2018 generó revuelo en redes sociales y medios de comunicación, reabriendo el debate sobre el patrocinio comercial y la exposición pública de las deportistas de élite. A diferencia del contenido de carácter explícito que suele asociarse a la plataforma, la portera sevillana aclaró que utilizará este canal para ofrecer a sus seguidores una visión exclusiva de su día a día como profesional y de su vida cotidiana fuera del césped. "Estoy súper feliz de anunciaros que me uno a la familia de OnlyFans. Voy a compartir con vosotros lo que normalmente no veis: cómo entreno y me preparo para los partidos, mi día a día, la llegada de nuestro bebé y muchas otras cosas sobre mi vida personal y profesional que me acercarán un poquito más a vosotros", expresó Gallardo a través de sus redes. Entre los contenidos anunciados por la guardameta destacan: La incursión de la capitana rojiblanca ha suscitado opiniones encontradas en el ámbito mediático y en las plataformas digitales: Lola Gallardo es una de las figuras más emblemáticas del fútbol femenino español en la última década. Como capitana e histórica referente del Atlético de Madrid, ha conquistado títulos de liga y Copa de la Reina. Además, ha sido una de las voces más firmes en las reivindicaciones de mejoras en la Real Federación Española de Fútbol (RFEF) y el desarrollo del fútbol profesional femenino.

articles.title: La historia no contada del FACSAT-2: El único satélite de Colombia se desintegró dos años antes de lo previsto
articles.standfirst: Detalles inéditos sobre el proyecto espacial colombiano que no logró cumplir su ciclo y la verdad detrás de su pérdida en la órbita
articles.summary: Detalles inéditos sobre el proyecto espacial colombiano que no logró cumplir su ciclo y la verdad detrás de su pérdida en la órbita
articles.body: En abril de 2023, Colombia celebró con entusiasmo el lanzamiento del FACSAT-2 "Chiribiquete", un nanosatélite de última generación enviado al espacio a bordo de un cohete Falcon 9 de SpaceX. El proyecto, anunciado con orgullo por la Fuerza Aeroespacial Colombiana (FAC) y exaltado en su momento por el presidente Gustavo Petro, prometía convertirse en un pilar fundamental para el monitoreo ambiental, la detección de gases de efecto invernadero junto a Ecopetrol y la seguridad nacional. Sin embargo, detrás del optimismo institucional se escondía un desenlace prematuro que permaneció en la sombra. De acuerdo con un seguimiento exclusivo realizado por El Tiempo, el único satélite operativo del país se salió de órbita y se desintegró en la atmósfera terrestre el 27 de octubre de 2025, apenas 30 meses después de su lanzamiento. Al artefacto le restaban, según los cálculos más pesimistas, al menos dos años y medio más de misión y más de doce años de permanencia en órbita. La revelación del fin de la misión no provino de un parte oficial del Gobierno, sino de la comunidad científica. Un estudio publicado en la plataforma académica arXiv y liderado por Santiago Vargas, docente del Observatorio Astronómico Nacional de la Universidad Nacional de Colombia, detalló cómo y por qué el nanosatélite perdió altura mucho más rápido de lo proyectado. Utilizando bases de datos internacionales de rastreo espacial como Space-Track y CelesTrak, los investigadores determinaron que el factor determinante fue la intensa actividad del Sol durante el Ciclo Solar 25. "El Sol fue mucho más activo de lo que se pronosticaba cuando se diseñó la misión, lo que llevó a que la atmósfera terrestre se expandiera y aumentara el frenado sobre los satélites (...). A esto se suman las tormentas geomagnéticas, como la tormenta Gannon de mayo de 2024, la más intensa en dos décadas", explicó el profesor Vargas en la investigación. Según el análisis, esta sobreactividad atmosférica redujo la vida del FACSAT-2 casi a la mitad de su tiempo operativo previsto. A pesar de que la comunicación con el satélite cesó en octubre de 2025 y su desintegración se confirmó analíticamente poco después, las plataformas oficiales de la Fuerza Aeroespacial y del Ministerio de Defensa continuaron publicando boletines donde aseguraban que el FACSAT-2 seguía en funcionamiento. En notas institucionales difundidas a finales de 2025 e incluso consultadas meses después, la FAC afirmaba que la plataforma continuaba "aportando información geoespacial clave para la seguridad, la gestión del riesgo y la investigación científica", habiendo completado cerca de 12.800 órbitas. Ante el requerimiento mediante derecho de petición, la FAC argumentó que siempre tuvo conocimiento del estado del artefacto y que el fin de la misión respondió a un proceso normal de reentrada atmosférica propio del paradigma New Space, el cual promueve misiones cortas en órbita baja para reducir costos y evitar la acumulación de basura espacial. Sin embargo, expertos de la comunidad académica señalaron inconsistencias en esta explicación, recordando que la FAC ya había documentado en estudios de 2021 cómo la actividad solar aceleraba el decaimiento orbital, por lo que atribuir el evento de forma tardía a una filosofía de "misión corta" resulta contradictorio. En su respuesta, la FAC sostuvo que notificó formalmente el fin de la misión a la Oficina de las Naciones Unidas para los Asuntos del Espacio Exterior (UNOOSA) a través de la Cancillería. No obstante, la falta de un anuncio público dentro del territorio nacional generó cuestionamientos frente a la Ley de Transparencia y Acceso a la Información Pública (Ley 1712 de 2014), la cual exige a las entidades estatales divulgar de manera proactiva los hechos de interés público. El FACSAT-2 contó con un lente multiespectral de alta resolución (4,7 metros por píxel) y un espectrómetro infrarrojo destinado a rastrear emisiones de dióxido de carbono y metano. Aunque su paso por el espacio dejó aprendizajes valiosos y capacidades operativas consolidadas en el Centro de Operaciones Espaciales (SpOC) de Cali, su silencioso final deja al país temporalmente sin un satélite propio en órbita, a la espera del desarrollo del futuro programa FACSAT-III.

articles.title: Why Max Verstappen says 0.196s Baku finish-line gap to George Russell is slightly misleading
articles.summary: Verstappen says the true margin was a full second and adds that victory would have been difficult even without the engine problem in qualifying. For one of t...
articles.body:
At the Baku City Circuit, the words Russell spoke after qualifying became reality: the Mercedes driver had already predicted on Friday that, despite starting eighth, Verstappen would pose the biggest threat for victory, and that proved to be the case in a thrilling finale around the streets of Baku.

Verstappen fell just 0.196 seconds short of his first victory of the 2026 Formula 1 season at the line, although he stressed afterwards that the actual gap was slightly larger than that.

"Of course, it looked close on the line, but I think that was more because George suffered from a little bit of boost lag in Turn 15 with the yellow flag", Verstappen said.

"So if you look at the last stint, it was always one second, so that's probably also where we would have finished."

It is a theory that Russell himself also confirms. After lifting off for Valtteri Bottas ' crash, the Mercedes power unit did not immediately deliver the acceleration he was expecting.

"When the yellow flag came out, I lifted off the power and when I went back on, I had no turbo, so then I had no power", the Mercedes driver explained. "Max almost got me at the line. That would have been a real shame, but all in all, it's been an incredible weekend."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, George Russell, Mercedes

Verstappen also believes the outcome of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix would have been the same had he started from the front row.

On Friday, the four-time world champion concluded that Red Bull had "done a great job messing up" its best chance of a victory this year with the engine problem, but 24 hours later Verstappen believes the closing stages of the race would have played out in more or less the same way.

"I mean, that's what happened yesterday. You have a problem and that means that you have to start from P8. But I think even if I started second, I think with the pace of George, it would have been very hard to pass", the Dutchman admitted.

"So maybe I could have followed him a bit better in that first stint, of course. But then you box, you're second, and then we would probably have done the same race, just pushing each other along."

Verstappen able to enjoy F1 for one of the first times in 2026

Verstappen does, however, say that he enjoyed the closing stages in Baku, which, given all the shortcomings of the technical regulations, was one of the first times he had done so all year.

"I have to say that those last laps were very enjoyable because there was barely any deg, really. We were just pushing to the end and the gap was always, like, one second or 1.1. That was nice."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

Verstappen also took risks in that respect, risks he perhaps would not have taken for any result other than a potential race win. He knew Red Bull – especially with overtake mode – had an impressive amount of top speed, while Mercedes was faster in the twisty section around Baku's old town.

To still give himself a chance on the longest straight of the F1 calendar and at least close the gap again on every lap, Verstappen tried to 'open up' the final few corners as much as possible.

"That last stint was fun. I kissed a few walls as well, but that was just to leave my mark here in Baku!", Verstappen smiled.

"So, yeah, it's always very challenging around here, qualifying and now at the end of the race as well, just pushing flat out. That comes with risk, of course, being close to certain walls on the inside and the outside, but it was cool."

articles.title: Evangel, Haughton, Ruston, BTW among Friday Shreveport area winners
articles.summary: Loyola and Northwood combined for over 1,100 yards while Ruston and Haughton secured big wins in Friday action.
articles.body:
We knew the late Jerry Burton pretty well and he would have been freaked out by the offensive numbers posted Sept. 25 by Loyola and Northwood in the stadium that bears his name.

The two rivals combined for 1,105 yards almost evenly split between the two, although the Flyers (3-1) won the point battle 71-59 versus the Falcons (1-3). Loyola's Bryce Restovich, perhaps the best quarterback in the state without a major Division I offer, completed 21 of 31 throws for 424 yards and six touchdowns without an interception. He also rushed for 64 yards and another score. Sure-handed Charlie McKenzie hauled in 8 passes for 137 yards and two scores with Ty Walsworth catching 7 for 133 and two TDs.

On flipside, Northwood's Peyton Boone rushed for two scores and passed for a third, while Caden Stewart rushed 22 times for 150 yards and three scores.

The offensive onslaught made for a long night in Jerry Burton Memorial Stadium.

Ruston 63, Catholic-B.R. 28: Apparently you don't want to catch Ruston (3-1) following a loss. A week after losing on the road to Karr, the Bearcats blew past the Bears (1-3) behind quarterback Sam Hartwell, who completed 17 of 27 passes for 316 yards and five TDs, while rushing for 162 more yards and another score. Ruston's Kohl Gray added 146 yards on 16 totes with three TDs.

Haughton 50, Captain Shreve 36: The Buccaneers (4-0) remained undefeated with a dominant win versus the Gators (2-2). Brandon Craig rushed 25 times for 186 yards and four TDs, while Taylor Weathersby completed 14 of 25 passes for 371 yards and three scores for Haughton. Ethan Johnson caught 7 passes for 131 yards and two TDs. For Shreve, Gabe Lockett rushed 21 times for 214 yards and two TDs, while Maddox Parrot passed for 323 yards and three TDs (career highs). Kaleb Law snared 7 passes for 131 yards and two TDs.

articles.title: England's Harrison scores last-gasp try to beat Black Ferns
articles.summary: Zoe Harrison scores last-gasp try as England defeat New Zealand at Allianz Stadium to avoid a second successive draw in the WXV Global Series.
articles.body:
Tries: Moloney-MacDonald, Kildunne, Breach, Harrison Cons: Harrison 3

Tries: Du Plessis, Leti-I'iga, Paul Con: Sorensen-McGee 2

Zoe Harrison scored a last-gasp try as England defeated New Zealand at Allianz Stadium to avoid a second successive draw in the WXV Global Series.

With the scores level at 19-19 in the 81st minute and having missed a penalty moments earlier, Harrison intercepted a pass as the Black Ferns tried to counter-attack, the fly-half diving over the line and piled up on by celebrating team-mates.

The world champions' record 39-game winning run came to an end last weekend in the 26-26 draw with Canada , but this week they were able to find a dramatic path to victory, much to the delight of the 59,871 crowd.

New Zealand, the last team to beat England in the World Cup final in 2022, suffered their first defeat under new head coach Whitney Hansen.

The Black Ferns had taken a deserved lead at half-time after tries from Amy du Plessis and Ayesha Leti-I'iga ruled out Claudia Moloney-MacDonald's opening score.

Tries by Ellie Kildunne and Jess Breach restored John Mitchell's side's lead, before Mererangi Paul's converted try drew the game level on 70 minutes.

England now travel to Canada to complete their three-Test series against the World Cup finalists in Toronto and Ottawa, while the Black Ferns play France in Hamilton.

The Black Ferns have beaten the Red Roses in all five World Cup final meetings they have contested.

Canada outclassed New Zealand in last year's World Cup semi-final to deny a repeat of what is one of rugby's great rivalries.

Under Hansen, who took over as head coach after last year's disappointing World Cup, the Black Ferns were unbeaten and have defeated Canada and France this year.

The world's second-ranked side spent a large chunk of the first half deep in England's 22, and an opportunistic kick found unmarked space for Du Plessis to dot down for a deserved try.

England comfortably beat New Zealand 49-31 in their most recent meeting in 2024, winning all three encounters since their 2022 World Cup final defeat, which has opened the door for Canada to become the Red Roses' toughest contest.

However, the years were rolled back in Twickenham as Hansen's side brought a fearsome level of physicality and speed to challenge the Red Roses.

Leti-I'iga, who had an opening try ruled out, caused havoc throughout the first half and finally crossed after Tyla King broke clear, before a poorly judged cross-field kick, with another try beckoning, let Mitchell's side off the hook.

articles.title: Wigan Warriors 6-33 Wakefield Trinity: Daryl Powell's side through to Super League Grand Final after producing major upset
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity booked their place in their first-ever Super League Grand Final on Saturday night as they produced a huge upset to defeat Wigan Warriors 33-6; watch Warrington vs Wakefield in the Super League Grand Final live on Sky Sports Main Event
articles.body:
League Leaders Shield winners Wigan had not lost in their last 16 games across all competitions, and were hot favourites to advance to their third-straight Super League Grand Final, but they were left stunned by a ferocious Wakefield team, who, had been playing their rugby in the Championship two years ago.

After a cagey first half, the visitors capitalised on what would be a costly second-half sin bin for Warriors playmaker Adam Keighan, running in a trio of tries from Tom Johnstone, Jack Sinfield and Corey Hall inside seven minutes as they romped their way to a 27-point victory.

"I thought we were superb," Wakefield head coach Daryl Powell said. "We completed at 100 per cent in the second half, 94 per cent in the first half. We made one error all game.

"Wigan are excellent, and they've had an unbelievable season, but I thought we were unbelievable tonight. We started a little bit shaky but once we got our teeth into the game

"It's a special group of boys and we've got an amazing opportunity next week now."

The first half was a cagey affair, with both sides matching each other's intensity, but it would be Wigan who would take the advantage first after Trinity's Jazz Tevaga was sent to the sin bin for a trip on Liam Marshall.

Brad O'Neill made the visitors pay, bulldozing his way over, but Wakefield hit back through Johnstone, who finished off a superb move in the corner.

Wigan lacked discipline at times, and a penalty right in front of the posts for a ruck infringement saw Trinity take a two-point advantage heading into the break.

The second half continued with the same intensity, with neither side able to pull away.

But a tip-tackle from Keighran on Isaiah Vagana proved a decisive moment, with the Warriors five-eighth being shown a yellow card.

Wakefield immediately attacked, with Johnstone capitalising on a mismatched defence, crossing over in the corner with another sensational finish, before Sinfield bulldozed his way past Junior Nsemba for another try moments later.

Powell's side had a third within seven minutes of Keighran's sin bin, with Hall flying down the wing before crossing the finish line.

Jake Trueman was brilliant throughout the match, and popped off a lovely offload to Ky Rodwell, who crashed over for the final try of the match.

"They had to be very good to punish us when we lost Adam [Keighran]," Wigan Warriors head coach Matty Peet said on Keighran's sin bin.

"No way is this game about that. We were well beaten. Wakefield deserve it. We were well prepared, we were motivated but they were too good.

"I can see why it was given, there's always opinions, but this game's not about that."

"Credit to Wakefield, it hurts, but the night belongs to them."

articles.title: Trump’s visit to Texas-Tennessee game could interrupt coaches’ headsets, they warn
articles.summary: Encouraging fans to get inside Neyland Stadium earlier than usual with President Donald Trump coming to Tennessee’s college football game against Texas sure worked Saturday.
articles.body: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. — Encouraging fans to get inside Neyland Stadium earlier than usual with President Donald Trump coming to Tennessee’s college football game against Texas sure worked Saturday. Security checks on the stadium’s perimeter went relatively smoothly with Tennessee officials opening the stadium 30 minutes earlier than normal. Fans got half-price off concessions as a reward for showing up early, and Tennessee faithful had the stands half full 90 minutes before kickoff and nearly packed an hour before. Those in their seats were treated to a low-altitude flyover by Air Force One as the president came into town with the Volunteers and Longhorns warming up on the field below. Trump landed at 11:28 a.m. ET ahead of the noon kickoff, according to the pool report. The bigger disruptions from Trump’s visit could go all the way to the game on the field, with headaches for coaches and players, Longhorns coach Steve Sarkisian said this week. The Southeastern Conference matchup between the No. 1 Longhorns and No. 14 Volunteers in Knoxville already was one of the biggest games in the country this weekend. Trump came to watch Texas quarterback Arch Manning play for the first time in the stadium where his uncle Peyton became famous. And what Trump does, and where he goes and when, could prove important. Teams must be ready to lose all communication on their headsets between coaches on the field and the players “anytime (Trump) enters the stadium, leaves the stadium or changes locations within the stadium,” Sarkisian said. “They cut the headsets to coaches. They cut headsets for coach-to-player communication. So you have to have a plan for that, if and when it happens, and you get no warning. It just gets cut out,” Sarkisian said. And “anytime” really means anytime. “You have to have a plan to adjust if and when he comes in the middle of the first quarter, leaves in the fourth quarter, or decides he’s got to use the restroom,” Sarkisian said. How a presidential visit can affect radio communications Trump has attended more college football games than any recent sitting president, and he arrived in Knoxville in the midst of a midterm election season and a heated debate over the role of money in college sports that Congress is trying to resolve. He has attended national championship games and regular season contests in the SEC and Army vs. Navy. He also attended Game 3 of the NBA finals between the New York Knicks and San Antonio Spurs in June, went to the 2025 Daytona 500 car race, and presented the World Cup trophy to Spain at the final in July. And last year, he was the first president to attend a Super Bowl. He left the Super Bowl after halftime. Headset communications emerged as the latest subplot surrounding this presidential visit. Coaches communicate with each other on their headsets throughout the game and also call in plays to the quarterback. Disruptions to those communications, from a deafening crowd, technical glitch or presidential security measure, can present problems for coaches and teams. Coaches involved in last season’s College Football Playoff championship between Miami and Indiana in New Orleans cited that game as an example of how Trump’s movements affected them. Trump left in the fourth quarter of a tense Indiana 27-21 victory. Sarkisian said Miami coach Mario Cristobal told him Trump’s leaving at that point disrupted communications on the Hurricanes’ final possession, which ended with a game-clinching interception. Indiana coach Curt Signetti disputed Sarkisian’s version of events around the final drive. But Cignetti noted communications briefly cut off in a key moment of the fourth quarter as Indiana was trying to protect its lead. In his weekly radio show on Thursday, Cignetti recalled that when Trump left the game “around the 7-minute mark ... there were two or three plays we couldn’t hear at all.” That included a misdirection touchdown run by Miami’s Malachi Toney. “Communication device came back right after the (Toney’s) touchdown,” Cignetti said. “And we had no problem the rest of the game.” According to the media pool report of Trump’s movements at the game, the president left the stadium with “with just under 8 minutes left in the 4th quarter.” The White House on Friday insisted Trump’s departure caused no problems for the teams. “No, President Trump’s departure from the CFP championship in January did not cause headset or comms issues for the teams,” the White House posted on X. It’s unclear if Trump’s presence at other games like the Super Bowl have created issues. An NFL spokesman declined comment Friday when asked if league officials work with the Secret Service when a president attends a game like the Super Bowl to minimize any impact on team communications. Trump’s visit to Neyland Stadium University of Tennessee officials sent a midweek advisory encouraging fans to arrive “significantly earlier” than for a typical game. Neyland Stadium has an official capacity of 101,915 with this game the 30th consecutive sellout. Fans were warned of the Secret Service conducting enhanced screening at the stadium gates and to “expect increased wait times as kickoff approaches.”

Beaugrand won comfortably, completing the 1.5km swim, 40km bike ride and 10km run in one hour 50 minutes 52 seconds, which was over a minute quicker than Taylor-Brown.

Potter, who won the World Series at Pontevedra in 2023, remained in contention at the end of the cycle, but Beaugrand stretched clear of the three Brits in the second lap of the run and held firm.

It concludes a dominant season for Beaugrand, who has won all five of the World Championship circuit races she entered.

articles.title: Wakefield Trinity reach Super League Grand Final two years after promotion from second tier
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity were playing in rugby league's second tier in 2024. Two years on, they are one win away from becoming Super League champions.
articles.body:
"It's something I've dreamed about for years and it used to be a bit of a pipe dream," said Tom Johnstone, when asked about the prospect of Wakefield Trinity winning a Super League Grand Final.

That dream could become a reality for the England winger on 3 October, after Wakefield shocked treble-chasing Wigan Warriors 33-6 in Saturday's play-off semi-final to secure their place in the Old Trafford showpiece for the first time.

Wakefield, who will play Warrington Wolves in the title decider, have been a club transformed in recent seasons.

So often competing at the wrong end of the Super League table, they lost their top-flight status in 2023 - but that proved to be the beginning of the club's reinvigoration, sparked by the completion of a takeover by kitchen magnate Matt Ellis.

His financial support, along with the leadership and experience of head coach Daryl Powell, have led Wakefield up from the Championship and now to within 80 minutes of becoming Super League champions.

Johnstone, 31, began his career with Wakefield and was back for Trinity's return to the top division at the start of 2025 after a two-year spell with Catalans Dragons.

"I went to Matt's kitchen factory with my agent and we had a chat about everything they want to achieve and everything they promised to do," Johnstone, who scored two of Wakefield's five tries against Wigan, told BBC Two.

"We left and said: 'If they do any of that, it's going to be something special.' I couldn't say no."

Powell, who was appointed shortly after Wakefield had dropped into the second tier, added: "The journey's been an interesting one.

"We got relegated but it was probably good for us. It allowed us to stabilise the team, get our staff in and sign some players that got us out of the Championship.

"We started to sign high-quality players like Mike [McMeeken] and Tom, and some of the guys we signed the year before have really grown and prospered."

Wakefield shock Wigan to reach first Grand Final

Warrington edge past Leeds to reach Grand Final

'Definitely Wakefield's best ever performance in Super League'

Prior to the semi-final, many viewed Wakefield - who finished fourth in Super League - as second favourites against a Wigan team that had won 16 successive matches and were seeking a second domestic treble in the space of three seasons.

But Trinity responded brilliantly to falling behind early on and took full advantage of Adam Keighran's second-half yellow card, seizing control of the contest and winning it with 33 unanswered points.

Ex-England half-back Kevin Brown, working as a BBC pundit, described Wakefield's display against Wigan as "definitely their best ever performance in Super League", adding: "It's been an incredible story where we're at right now and we're going to run out of superlatives if they go and win it."

Captain McMeeken has played in three previous Grand Finals with Castleford and Catalans, while he was also part of the England side that played in a World Cup semi-final on home soil in 2022 - but the significance of Saturday's achievement was not lost on him, either.

"To take in an experience like this is up there as one of the best moments of my career so far," he said.

At Old Trafford, Powell will come up against the club he coached for a season and a half before his exit midway through the 2023 campaign.

He said: "It's not about me or my journey, it's about the players and how they're writing different scripts every time we take the field."

Whoever is victorious will be a first-time Super League champion and Powell added: "It'll be awesome for the game. I think it's awesome that we're there in particular, Warrington have been there before.

"For us, it's about not getting too ahead of ourselves, playing the game as it is like we did tonight, and if we do that, we've got a great chance."

Alex Bregman returned just in time for the Chicago Cubs . His place in Friday's lineup also created a question Craig Counsell must answer before the Wild Card Series: If Bregman needs the designated hitter spot, which other bat loses at-bats?

Bregman started at DH and hit third in the first game against Boston. It was his first appearance since a foul ball struck his face Sunday and caused multiple fractures. He went 0-for-4 in Chicago's 4-3 loss, then did not start the nightcap.

The DH assignment allowed Matt Shaw to stay at third base in the opener. Michael Conforto , who has drawn DH starts, was absent from that starting lineup. Those choices offer an early glimpse of a roster squeeze, although Friday's doubleheader required Counsell to manage two games in one day. That distinction matters before drawing conclusions about his playoff plan.

The Game 2 box score shows a different lineup. Conforto started at DH, and Shaw remained at third while Bregman sat. Conforto went hitless in four at-bats during the 2-0 defeat.

That does not mean Conforto has been dropped for October. It does show why Bregman's defensive availability matters. If he can return to third base, Counsell can keep a DH opening for Conforto or another hitter and decide where Shaw provides the most value.

If Bregman stays at DH, those choices narrow. Shaw could play third, but someone who otherwise might have occupied the DH spot would need another place in the field or a bench role. Chicago has a short series ahead, leaving limited time to wait for a struggling lineup combination to settle.

Bregman told MLB.com after his return that his face felt fine during the game. The Cubs said team doctors cleared him after vision testing and an evaluation that found surgery unnecessary. Neither point is an announcement that he will play third base Tuesday.

The final regular-season game against Boston gives Counsell one more opportunity to arrange the infield and DH spot before the Wild Card opener. The starting card could be informative, though an individual day's rest plan would not settle the postseason order.

MLB's Cubs postseason FAQ projects Bregman at third and lists Conforto and Shaw among the bench options. MLB describes that roster as a projection, not a team announcement. Friday's two lineups showed how quickly the actual alignment can change.

Chicago scored three runs across Friday's two games and none in the second. That makes the decision about more than who wears a glove. Counsell needs Bregman's bat available, but he also needs the rest of his lineup to produce.

The biggest unanswered question is straightforward: Can Bregman play third when the playoffs begin? Until the Cubs confirm the plan, Conforto's role and Shaw's starting opportunity remain up in the air. Sunday's lineup could sharpen the picture; Tuesday's postseason card will provide the answer.

articles.title: Steelers Linebacker Fined for Penalty vs. Patriots
articles.summary: Pittsburgh Steelers inside linebacker Payton Wilson was fined for a fourth-quarter facemask penalty in Week 2’s 20-3 loss to the […]
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers inside linebacker Payton Wilson was fined for a fourth-quarter facemask penalty in Week 2's 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots.

Wilson was flagged for the foul, which occurred with 1:13 remaining of the fourth quarter of a 20-3 New England victory.

Wilson was attempting to tackle Patriots running back Corey Kiner when he was blocked in the back by offensive lineman Caleb Lomu. Wilson's left hand grabbed Kiner's facemask, and Wilson swung Kiner's body around by the facemask as Jaquan Brisker and Nick Herbig closed to make the tackle.

#Steelers LB Payton Wilson was fined $8,480 for this facemask penalty late in the Week 2 loss to the #Patriots pic.twitter.com/mg1hMgvJX7 — Josh Carney (@ByJoshCarney) September 26, 2026

#Steelers LB Payton Wilson was fined $8,480 for this facemask penalty late in the Week 2 loss to the #Patriots pic.twitter.com/mg1hMgvJX7

Josh Carney (@ByJoshCarney) September 26, 2026

On Saturday, the NFL announced its fines for Week 2, and Wilson was hit with a $8,480 monetary penalty for the foul, in addition to the 15 yards.

The fine was the first for Wilson this season and the first for any Steelers player this regular season. Cornerback Doneiko Slaughter was fined $4,917 for taunting in Week 3 of the preseason.

No Patriots players were fined for their actions in the game.

Wilson is entering the third season of his four-year rookie contract. He is set to earn $1.304 million in salary this season.

The Steelers have been one of the most-fined teams in the league in each of the last three seasons.

The Steelers were the second-most fined NFL team in 2025 , racking up $749,747 in fines, over 18 total infractions according to date from The Action Network. Only the Washington Commanders were fined more.

They were the third-most fined team in the NFL during the 2024 season, and were the most-fined team in the NFL in 2023 , with fines totaling $478,091.

articles.body:
Justin Ellis has just lived out every young footballer's dream — scoring on his national team debut in his home city.

The Orlando City forward was given his first USMNT start in front of the Orlando crowd by Mauricio Pochettino, and he rewarded the manager in less than five minutes.

After a quick start from the home side, Ellis nodded home a looping header to the back-post off of a Gio Reyna set-piece.

Ellis has been one of the best stories in MLS this season, bagging a goal and nine assists since making the jump up from the Orlando City second team.

Now that is truly a moment he will never forget.

articles.title: Lehigh beats Penn 20-7 for 5th consecutive win against an Ivy League opponent
articles.summary: Derek Morgan threw for a touchdown and ran for another to guide Lehigh to a 20-7 victory over Pennsylvania on Saturday.  Lehigh (5-0), ranked No. 6 in the St...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Derek Morgan threw for a touchdown and ran for another to guide Lehigh to a 20-7 victory over Pennsylvania on Saturday.

Lehigh (5-0), ranked No. 6 in the Stats Perform poll, has won five consecutive games against Ivy League opponents and six of the last seven.

Morgan broke several tackles on his 11-yard scoring run that gave Lehigh a 10-0 lead in the third quarter following a four-play, 28-yard drive. He added a 20-yard scoring pass to Jamaire Harden — his first career touchdown — with 2:08 remaining in the frame for a 17-0 lead.

Connor Poole made field goals from 48 and 29 yards.

Luke Yoder, who entered ranked second nationally in rushing yards and first with 12 touchdowns, was held out of the end zone on 19 carries for 74 yards for Lehigh. The Mountain Hawks entered leading the FCS in rushing offense at 291.8 yards per game and finished with 168 yards on 47 attempts.

Freshman Miles Teodecki was 18 of 37 for 133 yards with two interceptions for Penn (1-1), which opened its 150th season of football with a 20-7 win at Bucknell last week. Tommy Lafayette had 41 yards rushing and a touchdown that came with 2:14 left in the fourth quarter.

The two teams combined for 399 yards and 26 first downs.

Lehigh was coming off a 24-20 victory over Dartmouth last week, highlighted by DJ Brown 's one-handed interception at the Mountain Hawks' 5-yard line with 13 seconds remaining to secure the victory.

Lehigh: Returns home to play Fordham next Saturday.

articles.title: Noah Gragson Shares Sad News of Grandfather’s Passing
articles.summary: Noah Gragson is carrying a heavy heart into Sunday’s NASCAR Cup Series Hollywood Casino 400 at Kansas Speedway. The driver of the No. 4 sadly announced the p...
articles.body:
Noah Gragson is carrying a heavy heart into Sunday's NASCAR Cup Series Hollywood Casino 400 at Kansas Speedway. The driver of the No. 4 sadly announced the passing of his grandfather, Ken, in a social media post on Friday.Gragson will roll off 21st for Sunday's race. The starting lineup for the Cup Series was set by the metric after the single-car qualifying session was canceled due to rain.

Noah Gragson reveals the passing of his grandfather

In a touching social media post, Gragson shared numerous photos of himself and his grandfather, commemorating the great times they had. Gragson said he has many fond memories of being around his grandfather, such as attending University of Las Vegas basketball games, card games and times together at the racetrack. Those are memories that Gragson said will stick with him forever."Love you grandpa Ken ♥️ from UNLV basketball games, playing cards during the summers in Laguna, cheering me on at the race track and everything in between. It's been a fun ride and memories I'll never forget. I love you and will miss you. See you on the other side pal ♥️," he wrote.The sad family news comes on the heels of Gragson finishing 16th in last Saturday's Cup Series Bass Pro Shops Night Race at Bristol Motor Speedway. Although the Front Row Motorsports driver had a three-race string of finishes outside the top 20 entering Bristol, positive results came prior to that.Gragson finished 17th in the Cup Series race at Iowa last August, then followed up with an 18th-place run at Richmond and a 10th-place result at New Hampshire. The 28-year-old recorded a season-best finish of ninth at Talladega last April.

Noah Gragson returning to Front Row Motorsports in 2027

It was announced last month that Gragson will return to the seat of the No. 4 Front Row Motorsports Ford in 2027 with options to extend beyond next year.In a statement released by FRM at the time, Gragson expressed optimism in the direction of his team's performance, adding that the chemistry with first-year crew chief Grant Hutchens is coming together. "I feel like we've kind of been turning a page, and I've been seeing a little bit of uptick in our performance, which is good, and working with first-year crew chief Grant, learning each other, it takes time, and I'm starting to see that page kind of turn in a sense of, hey, we're going back to race tracks for the second time now," Gragson said. "We know each other a little bit better now. I'm starting to see that progression these last couple weeks, and we've been working really hard behind the scenes to improve that team chemistry, that dynamic, the communication. This sport's all about people and having the right people around you, and I feel like I've got a great group around me. It's just we're trying to find what's the right direction we need to go in, and what will allow us to reach our full potential."After 29 races in 2026, Gragson ranks 31st in the points standings with two top-10 finishes and an average finish of 24.2.

articles.title: 4 reasons for optimism for Chargers against the Bills in Week 3
articles.summary: Here are four reasons to be optimistic about the Los Angeles Chargers picking up their first win of the season.
articles.body:
The Chargers enter the hardest part of their schedule with a Sunday showdown against the Bills , who are 2-0 behind fantastic play from quarterback Josh Allen .

Here are a few reasons to be optimistic that LA will upset Buffalo to get their first win.

The Bills have started the season 28th in defensive expected points added (EPA) per play allowed as they adjust to a new scheme under new coordinator Jim Leonhard . The defense has been particularly vulnerable against the pass, where they rank 30th in EPA/play allowed and have been shredded by Nico Collins and Amon-Ra St. Brown in two consecutive weeks. With Ladd McConkey fully practicing despite a rib injury, he should face little resistance to production. Buffalo is also only the third team in NFL history to start 2-0 while giving up 30 or more points in both games, so the Chargers may be able to score often, if not early, to ease some of their troubles regarding the offense.

Jacob Gibbs of the Beyond the Box Score podcast pointed out on Thursday that the Chargers offense under Mike McDaniel has been about as successful as the Jaguars and Bears were through the first two games of the Liam Coen and Ben Johnson eras, respectively. Those two offenses are now regarded as some of the best in the league and have raised the profiles of quarterbacks Trevor Lawrence and Caleb Williams to that of league-wide superstars. The McDaniel Chargers have actually been better at avoiding three-and-outs and have accrued a higher EPA/dropback and success rate on designed runs than either of those teams were in their first two games, but their -17.5 turnover EPA is nearly as much as the two of them accrued combined . Turnovers are generally volatile, suggesting LA should be able to get on track and that there's still hope they'll reach the heights fans expected when McDaniel was hired as offensive coordinator.

Despite playing both running backs selected in the top ten of the draft in the last two years, the Chargers are currently 7th in the NFL in rushing yards allowed at 86.5 and are 8th in defensive EPA/rush and 6th in defensive rushing success rate. That will come in handy against 2025 rushing champion James Cook , who has 192 yards this season despite being held to 57 in Week 1 against Houston . Josh Allen is also a threat in the run game - he's third in the NFL among quarterbacks with 92 rushing yards and has already ran for four touchdowns this season. Keeping Buffalo in third-and-long situations will give LA a fair shot at winning Sunday's game.

That run defense might be especially useful if Buffalo is missing receivers DJ Moore and Keon Coleman , who are both questionable. Moore is dealing with a shoulder injury, while Coleman has an ankle injury. Head coach Joe Brady told the Buffalo media that they "still feel good" about some players being able to suit up on Sunday despite not practicing earlier in the week, so it's still possible that one or both of Moore and Coleman could suit up. If not, Buffalo will be down to Khalil Shakir , former Charger Joshua Palmer , rookie fourth-round pick Skyler Bell, and potential practice squad elevations Greg Dortch , Trent Sherfield , Ja'Mori Maclin, and Stephen Gosnell.

articles.title: Mike Locksley buyout, contract details as Maryland Terrapins coach
articles.summary: Could the end be near for Maryland coach Mike Locksley?
articles.body:
Maryland tuned out the noise about coach Mike Locksley's future last year and retained him for an eighth season, resolving to invest more resources into their roster rather than spending on a new head coach.

Four games into 2026, that plan has already gone awry.

The Terrapins suffered one of the worst losses in program history on Saturday, falling 54-3 to UCLA at home and raising more questions than ever before about Locksley's future.

Here are the details on what it would cost Maryland to fire Locksley.

Maryland would owe $9.2 million to Locksley if he's fired during this calendar year, USA Today reported .

While the Terrapins certainly don't have the resources that college football's powerhouses do, that buyout figure isn't dramatic compared to some of the massive buyouts paid out last season across the country, including $54 million for Brian Kelly at LSU and nearly as much for James Franklin at Penn State.

Maryland may not be inclined to make a midseason change, but the Terrapins hit a new low against UCLA and have yet to beat a Power Four opponent this season with road trips to Nebraska and Ohio State next on the schedule.

Locksley is under contract through the 2028 season; he makes $6.4 million this year and is set to make $6.7 million in 2027, followed by $7 million in 2028.

Locksley has been Maryland's head coach since 2019. Hired away from Nick Saban's Alabama staff after the 2018 season, Locksley has only three winning seasons in College Park and went 4-8 in both 2024 and 2025.

articles.title: Kane's penalty miss proves costly as England lose to world champions Spain
articles.summary: World Cup winners Spain came from 2-1 down to defeat England 3-2 in the Nations League at Wembley with Harry Kane missing a penalty.The newly-crowned champio...
articles.body:
World Cup winners Spain came from 2-1 down to defeat England 3-2 in the Nations League at Wembley with Harry Kane missing a penalty.

The newly-crowned champions took the lead just two minutes into the game when Lamine Yamal robbed Marc Guéhi before finishing past James Trafford .

From that point on, Spain could easily have scored more with Trafford making a good save to deny Ferran Torres . The Paris Saint-Germain forward then had another excellent chance but again couldn't find a way to goal.

Spain's wastefulness was punished by the Three Lions in the 36th minute through a quick counter-attack. Nico Williams slipped as Spain were on the attack with Elliot Anderson finding Anthony Gordon whose lovely flick played Jude Bellingham through the middle.

The Real Madrid midfielder then returned the favour with a perfectly weighted pass for the Barcelona wideman who finished past the out-of-position Unai Simón.

Just a few minutes later, England were ahead. This time with Nico O'Reilly crossing in for Harry Kane whose header went in despite Marc Cucurella 's attempt to block it.

Shortly into the second half the home side were awarded a penalty when Rodri tripped Jude Bellingham – a decision that was only given after the referee was sent to the screen by VAR. Kane stepped up but slipped at the crucial moment with his effort then bouncing off the bar.

That miss seemed to galvanise Spain who levelled with an hour gone. Álex Baena, who had come off the bench about five minutes earlier, with a curling effort after O'Reilly's errant pass.

After levelling the score Baena then assisted with what turned out to be the winning goal as he fed in fellow substitute Mikel Oyarzabal in the 74th minute who lifted the ball over Trafford to make it 3-2 to the visitors.

Thomas Tuchel brought on Morgan Gibbs-White and Dominic Calvert-Lewin late on but neither could find an equaliser with England losing their first game of the new Nations League campaign.

articles.title: Tennessee football, Josh Heupel had no answer for Texas' defense in loss | Adams
articles.summary: Tennessee couldn't block Texas star pass rusher Colin Simmons, who had five of his team's 10 sacks. In fact, it struggled to block anybody.
articles.body:
A quarterback named Manning won for the first time in 29 years at Neyland Stadium on Sept. 26. But this 20-17 victory didn't trigger a Tennessee football celebration.

And No. 1 Texas ' victory had more to do with its defense than its quarterback.

Arch Manning , the nephew of former Vols All-American quarterback Peyton Manning, led Texas for a touchdown on its first possession. After that, the game was all about defense – on both sides.

Tennessee shut down Texas' running game. But a Tennessee offense that was averaging almost 300 yards rushing per game in three consecutive victories struggled terribly to make headway against Texas. The Vols finished with only 70 yards rushing.

Passing was as problematic as running for the Vols.

Freshman quarterback Faizon Brandon, who missed two first-half series with a right-shoulder injury, was pressured repeatedly and had trouble finding open receivers against Texas' talented secondary. When Brandon did have time on short routes, he too often threw low.

Tennessee's biggest offensive dilemma: It couldn't block the No. 1 player on the nation's No. 1 team. All-American pass rusher Colin Simmons had five of the Longhorns' 10 sacks.

The Vols stayed within striking distance due to a stout defense and a 57-yard punt return for a touchdown by Qua Moss. They sacked Manning six times and held the Longhorns to 61 yards rushing.

But their offense was practically non-existent until the Vols unleashed an 80-yard touchdown drive on their next-to-last possession – after Texas opted for a prevent defense with a 10-point lead. Brandon scrambled for a first down before capping the drive with a 30-yard touchdown pass to Mike Matthews .

Suddenly, the Vols had hope. They also had the ball after Ryan Wingo couldn't handle their onside kick.

But once the Vols recovered on their own 49, Texas' defense returned to its aggressive ways, and the Vols' offense looked as futile as ever.

Tennessee's offense was without offensive guard Wendell Moe most of the game after he suffered a first-quarter injury. But losing one guard couldn't account for the failures of Tennessee's offensive line, which was overwhelmed by Texas' elite defensive front except for the late touchdown drive.

The Longhorns repeatedly sabotaged themselves in the first half with seven penalties for 70 yards.

Texas penalties figured prominently in Tennessee's only first-half score. The Longhorns were flagged for roughing the passer on the Vols' first play. They handed the Vols another 15 yards when they interfered with wide receiver Radarious Jackson on a deep throw from Brandon.

Those mistakes were crucial in Tennessee's nine-play, 60-yard drive that ended with Cooper Ranvier's 33-yard field goal.

Texas' star pass rusher went out of his way to commit another first-half penalty, which looked premediated. After sacking Brandon, Simmons celebrated by simulating an act best executed in a restroom.

If not for the unsportsmanlike penalty, Texas could have pinned the Vols close to their goal line. Given a second chance, Tennessee drove all the way to the Texas 34-yard line before missing on a fourth-down pass.

Texas' defense didn't have a monopoly on penalties. As effective as Manning was throwing in the first half, he was penalized twice for advancing beyond the line of scrimmage before releasing a pass.

The Longhorns' errant play continued in the third quarter. Safety Bo Mascoe was called for his second pass interference on Tennessee's first possession of the half.

Minutes later, Texas was forced to settle for a field goal after a delay-of-game penalty on third down stalled its drive. Another penalty negated a long punt return.

The Longhorns finished with 11 penalties for 115 yards.

Will Muschamp still a huge Tennessee nemesis

One of the last guys Tennessee fans want to see on an opponent's sideline is Will Muschamp, Texas' defensive coordinator.

The Vols have a long history with him, and most of it has been bad. In his long SEC career, he has been a head coach at Florida and South Carolina . He also has been an assistant coach at Florida, LSU , and Georgia.

The common theme to all his job-hopping: He seldomy loses to Tennessee. In the past 20 games against the Vols, including Texas' victory, Muschamp is 18-2.

Vols keep coming up short against ranked teams

A bigger concern for the Vols than Muschamp: They can't beat the better teams on their schedule.

Tennessee has lost seven consecutive games against nationally ranked opponents. Its last victory came against Alabama in October of 2024.

Every time the Vols threatened to end that streak, Texas' defense was too much to overcome.

John Adams is a senior columnist. He may be reached at 865-342-6284 or john.adams@knoxnews.com.

articles.title: UCLA stays unbeaten with a 54-3 drubbing of hapless Maryland
articles.summary: Ta'Shawn James and Scooter Jackson returned interceptions for touchdowns in the third quarter, and UCLA dominated Maryland 54-3 on Saturday.  Wayne Knight ra...
articles.body:
COLLEGE PARK, Md. (AP) — Ta'Shawn James and Scooter Jackson returned interceptions for touchdowns in the third quarter, and UCLA dominated Maryland 54-3 on Saturday.

Wayne Knight ran for 100 yards and a touchdown for the Bruins , who enter their open date undefeated under new coach Bob Chesney. UCLA (4-0, 2-0 Big Ten) led 20-3 after the first half and then extended its margin as rain began to fall harder in the final two quarters.

After a loss last week to Virginia Tech , Maryland coach Michael Locksley entered the game under increasing pressure, and the Terrapins (2-2, 0-1) responded with a desultory showing. They tried to establish the run early on, when the weather wasn't that bad yet. That failed miserably, and Malik Washington threw four interceptions when Maryland tried to pass.

UCLA's first three touchdowns came on direct snaps to non-quarterbacks. Knight took one 45 yards for a touchdown on fourth-and-1 to open the scoring in the second quarter. Anthony Woods made it 14-0 with a 1-yard run off a direct snap, and the crowd was really disgruntled when Maryland's next drive began with two runs for minus-4 yards.

Jaivian Thomas ran 3 yards for a touchdown on a direct snap to make it 20-0.

James' interception return for a TD went 39 yards, and Jackson's was 65 yards after Washington and his receiver were clearly not on the same page.

Nico Iamaleava threw an 83-yard touchdown pass to Aidan Mizell in the fourth, and Troy Leigber added a 63-yard TD run.

UCLA: This wasn't the type of weather the Bruins usually see in California , but they handled it fine. So far Chesney has made the transition to a new coaching staff look seamless at UCLA.

Maryland: Wanting balance is understandable, but Maryland's attempts to establish the run left Washington in some difficult third-down situations. The Terps failed to convert their first nine third downs.

UCLA: Off next week before playing at Oregon on Oct. 10.

articles.title: Justin Verlander's final start ends with daughter making pitching change
articles.summary: Justin Verlander retired in an emotional final start at Comerica Park, walking off the mound with his daughter.
articles.body:
A.J. Hinch has made plenty of pitching changes, but Saturday, he gave this one to someone else.

After Pittsburgh Pirates second baseman Brandon Lowe popped out in the sixth inning Saturday, the Detroit Tigers manager signaled to the stands and Justin Verlander 's daughter, Genevieve, sprinted out to the mound to get her father.

Justin Verlander was already crying as she closed the gap to the mound quickly. He bent down and wrapped her up in a hug that lasted about 15 seconds as the crowd around him rose. When he stood back up, he took his daughter's hand and walked off the mound for a final time .

It was the final scene of a farewell that Verlander and the Tigers had been building toward since he announced his retirement in July.

After two decades that took him from Detroit to Houston , New York and San Francisco , the 43-year-old came home for one last start, his first at Comerica Park in a Tiger uniform since he was traded in 2017 and only his second of this injury-wrecked season. He leaves as one of the defining pitchers of his generation: three Cy Young Awards, 2011 MVP, Rookie of the Year, three no-hitters, two World Series titles and 3,560 strikeouts, eighth in major league history. Saturday, in the ballpark where it started, he got to go out on his own terms.

As he and his daughter walked off, the crowd and his teammates gave him a standing ovation. The Pirates stood in their dugout, clapping and watching history.

Justin Verlander makes final start to close Hall of Fame career

Verlander tipped his cap. His wife, Kate Upton, and their son, Bellamy met him on the dirt for more hugs. He high-fived his way down a line of teammates, tipped his cap again, took a deep breath through tears, waved, tipped his cap again and disappeared down the dugout stairs.

It was the second time in two days Genevieve had been part of the show. Before Friday night's game, she threw the ceremonial first pitch to her dad and put it right over the plate.

Verlander left with the Tigers trailing 2-0 after having allowed two solo home runs and striking out six in 5 1/3 innings. The Tigers rallied to take him off the hook. Eduardo Valencia's two-run home run in the bottom of the ninth gave Detroit a 4-3 win in Verlander's last game.

articles.title: How much will Arion Carter donate to cancer patients after Tennessee-Texas game?
articles.summary: KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WATE) — Tennessee may have lost their matchup against Texas, but there will be a win for cancer patients with Vols linebacker Arion Carter...
articles.body:
KNOXVILLE, Tenn. (WATE) — Tennessee may have lost their matchup against Texas , but there will be a win for cancer patients with Vols linebacker Arion Carter donating nearly $4,700.

With his donation Saturday, Carter will have made more than $12,000 in donations to help people with their cancer treatments in partnership with his mother Sheteka Alexander's nonprofit Girls in Real Life Situations.

Earlier this season, Carter said he would be donating $427 for each tackle he made this season, in response to his one-game suspension from the NCAA over a $427.48 flight purchased for him by an agent before the NFL Draft last year , which he later withdrew from because of an injury. Carter later paid the money for the ticket back.

Along with $427 for each tackle, Carter also pledged to donate:

$1,000 per interception or forced fumble

and $5,000 if he scores a defensive touchdown

During Saturday's game against Texas , Carter had his highest number of tackles for a single game so far this season. For his 11 tackles, Carter pledged to donate $4,697, on top of the $7,332 in pledged donations from Tennessee's matchups against Kennesaw State and Georgia Tech. That brings his total in pledged donations this season to $12,029.

Last season, Carter averaged 7.6 tackles per game despite battling a foot injury. In total, he has made 161 tackles, one interception, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery during his time with the Vols.
