articles.title: Rams put lengthy AFC winning streak on the line against Broncos
articles.summary: LA has won eight straight against the AFC, while Denver is looking for its 10th win in a row over the NFC
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams take a lengthy AFC winning streak into the Mile High City when they face the Denver Broncos Sunday night.

LA has an eight-game winning streak against the conference, which dates back to the 2024 campaign. The last time the Rams lost to an interconference foe came in 2024 at home against the Miami Dolphins . Miami won it 23-15.

Since that loss, here are the results of the Rams' last eight wins over AFC opponents:

Nov. 17, 2024 – at New England Patriots (28-22)

Dec. 8, 2024 – vs. Buffalo Bills (44-42)

Sept. 7, 2025 – vs. Houston Texans (14-9)

Sept. 14, 2025 – at Tennessee Titans (33-19)

Sept. 28, 2025 – vs. Indianapolis Colts (27-20)

Oct. 12, 2025 – at Baltimore Ravens (17-3)

Oct. 19, 2025 – at Jacksonville Jaguars in London (35-7)

Turf Show Times' Kenneth Arthur pointed out before last season that the Rams have a winning record against the AFC in the 17-game era . Their record is 17-8, which includes a perfect 5-0 mark against the conference in 2025.

LA is 9-1 in its last 10 matchups against the AFC. Overall, the Rams have quite a strong interconference record under Sean McVay, going 29-13 since he took over in 2017, including the Super Bowl win over the Bengals .

Broncos similarly have a lengthy interconference win streak on the line

The Rams aren't the only ones riding a long interconference win streak heading into Sunday's game. Denver is looking to win its 10th straight against the NFC, which caught Broncos coach Sean Payton off guard during media availability earlier this week.

While the Broncos and Rams don't face off very often, Denver has struggled to beat LA no matter who's coaching.

In the McVay era alone, the Broncos lost to the Rams in 2018 with Vance Joseph roaming the sidelines as head coach, and then again on Christmas 2022 with Nathaniel Hackett. Hackett was fired shortly after the game, undoubtedly merrying up the holiday for Broncos Country that year.

The Broncos are on a five-game losing streak in the series and haven't beaten the Rams since 2002. That could change, as Denver quarterback Bo Nix simply doesn't lose to NFC opponents. Okay, he has once — in his NFL debut against the Seattle Seahawks . After that, the Oregon product has gone through the conference with relative ease, save for a few comebacks here and there.

This week's game is a test for both the Rams and Broncos as the two Super Bowl contenders have a lot on the line regarding interconference supremacy.

articles.title: Cowboys, Ravens strengths/weaknesses make for interesting matchup
articles.summary: The Cowboys passing game vs the Ravens running game is a big matchup
articles.body:
It's not very often two teams square off against one another and the strengths and weaknesses of both ball clubs align as they do in the Week 3 matchup between the Dallas Cowboys and Baltimore Ravens . Whichever team can best exploit this will likely be the one that walks away with the "W".

The Cowboys and Ravens currently find themselves in similar situations through the first two weeks of the 2026 NFL season. Both teams are 1-1 with a disappointing and unexpected loss under their belts, and yet, both still have Super Bowl aspirations. But there is still a lot of football left to play.

As we all know, the Cowboys biggest weakness so far through the first two weeks of the season this year is their run defense. They are currently ranked 30 th in the league allowing 173.5 rushing yards per game. On the flipside, the Ravens rushing attack is ranked fifth in the league, averaging 155 yards per game.

Baltimore's rushing attack, headlined by QB Lamar Jackson and RB Derrick Henry , could very well decide the outcome of this game. This is a tough duo to try to contain, especially Jackson, who may be arguably the best dual-threat QB in the history of the league. If Dallas can limit their production though, it could lead to victory.

The best chance for the Cowboys securing back-to-back wins is by exploiting the Ravens biggest weakness, their pass defense. Baltimore's currently allowing 191 passing yards a game, ranking 11 th in the league. That's not too shabby, but they have as of yet faced a team with the caliber of weapons Dak Prescott has at his disposal.

In CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens , the Cowboys All-Pro WR duo is arguably the best in the entire league. Then throw in Jake Ferguson and Ryan Flournoy , both of whom have strong chemistry with Prescott, and it becomes one of the more lethal units in the entire league. That could help even the playing field against the Ravens potent rushing attack.

Add it all up and this is one of those strengths versus weaknesses matchup's that could potentially go either way depending on which team is better exploits their opponent. And, considering both teams are playing at a neutral venue in Brazil, neither one has the edge of home field advantage, making this strength/weakness matchup all the more interesting.

articles.title: Donald Trump comments on Arch Manning, Protect College Sports Act in interview with Clay Travis
articles.summary: In August, Clay Travis launched Sport & State, which he billed as “70% sports, 15% pop culture, and 15% where politics intersects with sports.” “Most of the...
articles.body:
In August, Clay Travis launched Sport & State , which he billed as "70% sports, 15% pop culture, and 15% where politics intersects with sports."

"Most of the politics will come from me," Travis wrote in his first Sport & State column.

On Saturday, 100% of the politics came from President Donald Trump.

Travis previously reported Trump's plan to attend the No. 1 Texas Longhorns' matchup with the No. 14 Tennessee Volunteers at Neyland Stadium in Knoxville on Saturday afternoon.

Stephen A. Smith expressed concern that Trump would appear on ESPN's College GameDay and "use this moment to try to push forward the Protect College Sports Act ." Trump did not appear on GameDay , but Smith's overarching prediction came true.

Travis interviewed Trump for Sport & State at Neyland Stadium, and the controversial , bipartisan Protect College Sports Act was the first topic on deck.

"We actually had 78 votes, if you can believe it," Trump said, seemingly referencing the 74-24 procedural first vote on Sept. 15. "That's really bipartisanship for the first time in a while. And, I mean, the alternative is just no good. You had people leaving the NFL to play, and the colleges could never have afforded it. Nobody could afford it. It was gonna be a terrible thing."

"I think we've done a great job in putting it together," Trump continued. " We have to get it voted on , and we're counting on the House, and I think the House will come through, too."

Travis then asked for Trump's assessment of Texas quarterback Arch Manning.

"Well, he's already looking really good," Trump said. "I know the brothers, and they're fantastic. They're fantastic people and great quarterbacks and great football players. He's got great genetics, I would say. If you're gonna go for genetics, you can't do much better, and he's playing pretty well today."

The interview quickly devolved into meandering territory after that, to say the least, with Travis giving Trump the floor to say whatever he wanted, facts be damned.

Trump left the door open to meddling in a potential MLB lockout. For some reason, Travis asked him to weigh in on the worst sports trades of all time, which led to an unnecessary Dallas Cowboys history lesson.

Then, Travis abruptly pivoted into his wish for Trump to "go into Chicago and clean it up," giving Trump the floor to monologue about crime.

"We have the strongest, hottest country we've ever had economically. We have—you've probably heard the new numbers—21 trillion dollars being invested here," Trump claimed, which has been repeatedly fact-checked as false .

As soon as Travis broke the news that Trump would attend Saturday's game in Knoxville, speculation ran wild about whether or not he'd appear on GameDay . While ESPN was quick to put the kibosh on that , we should have figured that Travis would also have had the inside track on speaking with the President at some point.

articles.title: Lauren Coughlin makes nine straight birdies to post LPGA's lowest nine holes ever
articles.summary: Coughlin recorded the lowest nine-hole score in LPGA history, birdieing every hole of her opening nine and carding a 9-under 26 Saturday at the LPGA’s Walmar...
articles.body:
Lauren Coughlin recorded the lowest nine-hole score in LPGA history, birdieing every hole of her opening nine and carding a 9-under 26 Saturday at the LPGA's Walmart NW Arkansas Championship.

Coughlin, who opened the tournament in 2-over 73 on Friday, then parred her 10th hole, the par-4 first at Pinnacle Country Club in Rogers, Arkansas, to also tie the LPGA record for consecutive birdies.

Even with the record nine, Coughlin turned at 7 under for the tournament, nine shots off the lead at the time. Japan's Yuna Nishimura opened the event with back-to-back 63s.

The only other player in LPGA history to birdie every hole on a single nine was Amy Yang, who shot a 9-under 27 on her back nine of the final round of the 2015 LPGA KEB Hana Bank Championship. Yang was among five players who'd carded 27 for nine holes, though Mi Hyang Lee was the only other player to shoot 9 under (2016 Founders Cup).

The PGA Tour record for nine holes is 8-under 26, set by Corey Pavin at the 2006 U.S. Bank Championship. Jamie Kureluk's 11-under 25 at the 2010 Aberta Open still stands as the record in all competition.

Mark Calcavecchia and Kevin Chappell share the PGA Tour record for consecutive birdies with nine.

articles.title: Kolt Dieterich Has Proven to be a Critical Addition for Washington
articles.summary: Despite Jedd Fisch's emphasis on high school recruiting, landing Kolt Dieterich in the transfer portal has proven to be a big pickup for the offense.
articles.body:
During his time at Washington, Jedd Fisch has made it known that he wants to build his program through the high school recruiting ranks rather than depend on the transfer portal. The Huskies ' head coach has stuck to his word, putting together a trio of top-25 recruiting classes in 2025, 2026, and 2027.

However, one portal addition has slowly become one of their most important pieces on the offensive line. After three seasons at Sam Houston State, Kolt Dieterich made the move to Montlake as one of six offensive players the Huskies brought in through the portal this past offseason. Playing in 28 games for the Bearkats at both right and left tackle, the experienced lineman was thrust into a new position over the course of the offseason.

After starting center Landen Hatchett was scheduled to miss significant time following hand surgery in the spring, Fisch suggested moving the former tackle to center, a position he had never played at any point in his career. With Landen's brother, Geirean, also dealing with injuries, Dieterich took over as the starting center, as he has held his own ever since.

After struggling in his Husky debut against Washington State, the fourth-year player has seen improvements in his overall performance, jumping from a Pro Football Focus grade of 57.2 in the Apple Cup to 60.8 in his most recent showing against Eastern Washington.

Not only has the transfer been a help by filling in for the injured Hatchett, but it also provides additional depth to the room when the fourth-year center does return . Fisch and offensive line coach Michael Switzer have shown that they're not afraid to change their look up front throughout the game, as Geirean Hatchett and sophomore Champ Taulealea have split time at right guard, while starting left guard John Mills took a few series at left tackle in place of freshman Kodi Greene against EWU.

While most programs around the country would prefer to have a consistent front five at the line of scrimmage, Fisch and Switzer have welcomed the depth with open arms. With the current rotation being made up of six players, that number will move to seven once the younger Hatchett returns, giving Dieterich the luxury of moving back out to his natural position of tackle in times of need.

After struggling through a majority of the non-conference schedule, Washington will look to establish dominance up front against a Big Ten front in the Golden Gophers , who currently are ranked No. 59 in the nation in rush defense.

articles.title: Texans TE Dalton Schultz a must-start in fantasy with Nico Collins out
articles.summary: With Houston Texans wide receiver Nico Collins out versus the Indianapolis Colts, tight end Dalton Schultz is a must-start in fantasy football.
articles.body:
For the second week in a row, the Houston Texans will be without Pro Bowl wide receiver Nico Collins . For fantasy owners with tight end Dalton Schultz , this is actually a positive development as far as the kind of production he can have in this game.

Last week without Collins, Schultz was easily quarterback C.J. Stroud's favorite target with a total of 14 targets which he turned into 12 receptions for 140 yards. With the Texans going against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 3 as they try to get their first win of the year, this is an even better opportunity for Schultz to really help fantasy owners.

Indianapolis' defense has struggled throughout the first two games of the season, allowing over 500 total yards in each week as well as over 300 passing yards in those games. Furthermore, through the first two weeks, the Colts have given up the fourth-most fantasy points to tight ends. Everyone knows the ball is going to go to Dalton Schultz , but Indianapolis is not going to be able to stop them.

There are not many teams where the tight end is the top receiving target, which gives Schultz an advantage over every tight end in the NFL for fantasy purposes. He is also flying under the radar despite his breakout performance as he is still available in over 35 percent of ESPN fantasy leagues. So, if you have questions at tight end going into this week and Schultz is available in your league, pick him up and put him in your starting lineup for this game.

articles.title: 4 causes for concern for Chargers against the Bills in Week 3
articles.summary: Here are four reasons to be concerned about the Chargers falling to 0-3.
articles.body:
The Chargers enter the hardest part of their schedule with a Sunday showdown against the Bills , who are 2-0 behind fantastic play from quarterback Josh Allen .

Here are a few reasons to be concerned that LA will fall to 0-3 to start the year.

You could double the number of touchdowns the Chargers have scored this season (4) and still not reach the total Allen has piled up in two games (9) while leading the NFL's best offense. Buffalo 's 0.378 EPA/play on offense is 0.105 ahead of any other team - San Francisco is second at 0.273 - a difference that would rank ninth in the league if it were its own team. Allen has maintained his elite athleticism into his age-30 season, but is also processing coverages at the best level he ever has and has found nearly every throw available in Joe Brady's more aggressive version of the 2025 offense. The Chargers will be without safety Elijah Molden for a second straight game, which puts Tony Jefferson , RJ Mickens, and Genesis Smith on the clock to work out the miscommunications that led to several explosive plays for the Raiders last week.

David Njoku is on injured reserve. Charlie Kolar narrowly avoided IR after forearm surgery. Kayode Awosika and Trey Pipkins III are out. That leaves the Chargers with Oronde Gadsden II at tight end alongside Hayden Rucci , signed this week from the Jaguars ' practice squad after four games of experience with offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel in Miami last year, and practice squad elevation Patrick Herbert, who has never appeared in an NFL game. Trevor Penning is in line to start at left guard with Cole Strange at right guard. Meanwhile, in Buffalo, edge rusher Gregory Rousseau and defensive tackle Deone Walker have been off to All-Pro caliber starts, and star defensive tackle Ed Oliver could return from a hip injury this week. LA will have to rely on tackles Rashawn Slater and Joe Alt and fullback Alec Ingold to spring much of anything against that Bills front.

Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid has 12 catches for 225 yards and a touchdown through two games, one of the best starts for a tight end of anyone in the league. The Chargers struggled against a high-end receiver at the position in Week 1 when Cardinals tight end Trey McBride had 9 receptions for 95 yards and a touchdown. Safety Derwin James Jr. is now practicing in a cast after injuring his finger against the Raiders, but neither he nor linebacker Daiyan Henley have been at their best in coverage even before James was injured. They've combined to allow 12 receptions for 86 yards and 2 touchdowns in coverage this season and rank 195th and 216th of 267 players with at least 15 coverage snaps in PFF coverage grade. Buffalo can also utilize Dawson Knox and Jackson Hawes in the passing game, which makes a bounceback game for James and Henley all the more important.

Even before losing Njoku, Kolar, and Awosika, the Chargers' run game has been struggling, ranking 29th in yards before contact. 63.8% of LA's carries have resulted in contact at or behind the line of scrimmage, forcing Omarion Hampton to break tackles at a high rate just to claw to an early down success rate that ranks 16th in the league. Buffalo has been one of the league's worst run defenses through the first two weeks of the season, so it's possible Hampton and the run game can get on track, but that makes the losses up front sting even more as that possibility seems further off. Curiously, LA has also been a more effective gap-running team despite mostly employing outside zone runs in the first two games.

articles.title: Yang reveals hamstring concern as Celtic winger sets fitness goals
articles.summary: Celtic’s Yang Hyun-jun has revealed that a hamstring problem was behind his absence as South Korea advanced to the Asian Games semi-finals. The winger remain...
articles.body:
Celtic's Yang Hyun-jun has revealed that a hamstring problem was behind his absence as South Korea advanced to the Asian Games semi-finals. The winger remained unused during the 4-0 quarter-final victory over Vietnam , despite South Korea making all five substitutions.

Speaking after the game, Yang confirmed that his fitness had been compromised but that he retained an ambition to be fit for the last stages of the Asian Games.

"I have a minor injury to my hamstring," he said.

"Right now, I am preparing with the goal of reaching the semi-finals and the finals."

Yang also admitted his frustration at being unable to make the contribution he had hoped for after being selected as a wildcard player.

Hyunjun Yang of Celtic controls the ball during the Scottish Premiership 2026/27 match between Celtic and Dundee at Celtic Park on August 03, 2026. (Photo by Ian MacNicol/Getty Images)

"I was selected as a wild card, but since I haven't been in good physical condition recently and now I'm on top of that with an injury, I feel really sorry for my teammates. I also feel like I'm not being of any help.

"So I tried to be of even a little more help from the bench. I also check on their daily lives to see if they are experiencing any inconveniences, and I try to do whatever they need. The goal is a quick recovery."

The news gives Celtic another fitness situation to monitor during the international break, particularly following the uncertainty surrounding Haissem Hassan . The Egyptian star played 60 minutes after seemingly picking up an injury.

South Korea remain in contention for a fourth consecutive Asian Games football gold medal and Yang hopes to recover in time to feature in the closing stages.

Celtic will meanwhile want their winger returned to Glasgow fully fit rather than risk a minor hamstring complaint becoming a more substantial absence. Yang's absence has been felt over the last two weeks, suffering three defeats on the bounce. When Yang returns, he will likely face competition from Jota for a place in the Celtic starting XI, which might see him returning to the right wing.

articles.title: Box office Carlos Alcaraz edges Laver Cup classic with Taylor Fritz dramatics
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz and Taylor Fritz served up a Laver Cup classic as Team Europe drew level with Team World on Day 2.
articles.body:
LONDON — Carlos Alcaraz saved two match points in a scintillating tie-break to beat Taylor Fritz and draw Team Europe level in their quest to regain the Laver Cup.

With Team Europe being on the losing side in Saturday's morning session twice, team captain Yannick Noah turned to his world No. 3 for help, and boy, did he deliver and then some.

He ultimately avenged his Laver Cup defeat to Fritz last year with a 6-3, 4-6, 13-11 win to make it 5-5 between the two teams while putting on a show for a packed stadium.

Any fans lucky enough to get tickets for this year's Laver Cup at London's O2 would have been hoping to catch a glimpse of the seven-time grand slam champion in action. Getting him in the singles and a matchup against world No. 10 Fritz, too? Consider yourself winning the jackpot.

Alcaraz set the tone for this cracker, breaking Fritz in the first game and hitting a lovely lob over the 28-year-old in the second to establish some early dominance.

Fritz soon found his feet and broke back to level the score 3-3 before Alcaraz achieved break points once again in the seventh, this time a two-handed lob return after scrambling to the baseline to retrieve his opponent's attempted lob a standout highlight.

Fritz continued to find his groove in the second set though; breaking to love in the third game had his team fired up and unanimously gunning to take down the smiley Spaniard.

In truth, not many of the rallies were overly long, nor were they of the highest standard, but both players were hitting stunning winners into the corners, with Alcaraz chipping in with a few of his drop shot specialities.

Alcaraz broke Fritz's serve three times in the opening set, but the American had his serve locked down heading into the decisive match tiebreaker.

The duly named "Laver Breaker" was created to deliver a high-stakes 10-point tie-break to determine the winner of the third and final set. The likes of tournament creator Roger Federer, who was courtside for this one, could not have dreamt of a better tie-break with more drama.

It began with Alcaraz, as he usually does on the big stage, finding another gear when it mattered, saving some of his best shots until last. The deftest of drop shots to take a 5-1 lead had every one of his Team Europe colleagues on their feet.

A few nerves from Alcaraz crept in and saw him double fault, while some brilliant defensive play from Fritz left it level at 6-6. The pair continued to exchange blows and could hardly be separated as we reached 9-9. Two clear points were needed to determine a winner, and a raucous crowd was desperate for more. Alcaraz had them in the palm of his hand.

A backhand return into the net from Alcaraz gave Fritz match point, but the world No. 3 drilled an ace down the middle to save it. He then incredibly double-faulted to give Fritz a second match point on serve for even more drama. Alcaraz then held strong in a long rally to force Fritz into the mistake, 11-11. The crowd could not cope.

Alcaraz brought up his first match point with a trademark flick of the wrist forehand winner down the line. He'd now serve for the match and use his drop shot weapon in the final play to lure Fritz to the net with the American's return hitting the net.

Cue the loudest scream from the crowd all weekend and jubilant celebrations as a team.

The drama of the Laver Cup delivers once again.

articles.title: Highlights, MVP, and Twitter reactions to Kentucky’s win over South Alabama
articles.summary: Coming off a massive win vs. Texas A&M, Kentucky started slow vs. South Alabama but finished strong and got the win.
articles.body:
Early on, the hangover from the Texas A&M win was evident for Kentucky Football , which found itself trailing South Alabama after a start that left a lot to be desired. Thankfully, a strong end to the first half and a dominant second half pushed the Wildcats to a 45-21 win over the Jaguars.

Kentucky started this game with error after error, muffing a punt, turning it over on downs early, and digging itself a hole. The first half was back and forth, with Kentucky giving South Alabama good field position and then striking back on offense.

It looked like Kentucky would go into halftime down 21-14, but Jason Patterson had other plans. His response came on a 75-yard touchdown, led by a pancake block from Lance Heard, as he went untouched into the end zone. That would tie things up, then Grant Godfrey picked off South Alabama's Jared Hollins for the Jaguars' first turnover of the season. That would set up Adam Zouagui for a field goal to give Kentucky a slight lead at the break, 24-21.

The second half started exactly how you want it: four plays, 75 yards, and a touchdown. Three runs from CJ Baxter, and the touchdown run by Jason Patterson. That drive just about sums up the game; the running back room flipped the game on its head in the second half. Baxter, Patterson, and Jovantae Barnes were historically great in this one, with each of them finishing over the century mark in yards.

The entire second half looked much cleaner and much better overall. They took care of the ball, struck on early downs, and did not allow South Alabama to get any momentum. The passing game went from first-half drops to second-half catches and yards after the catch. I think it's safe to say, once again, the studs were fed.

We got what we wanted in this one, just took an unconventional route to get there. Kentucky was able to get backups in and let just about everyone they wanted into the game. Will Stein said he was "still not very happy" after the game, but a win is better than the alternative, and he covered the spread!

Patterson came into the day leading the team in rushing yards but had never found pay dirt through three games; that changed today. The junior running back would finish this game with a hat trick of touchdowns and 189 rushing yards on top of that.

Just giving him the MVP almost feels like I'm discrediting the running back room as a whole. The running back room combined for 399 yards and five touchdowns between five different running backs. The other two in the three-headed monster of a backfield were Baxter and Barnes. Baxter would finish the game with 149 yards and a touchdown, and Barnes would have 100 and a touchdown himself, his first as a Wildcat. Big shoutout to the offensive line for the elite blocking they provided throughout the day, especially in the second half.

articles.title: Five things we learned from Texas after 20-17 win over Tennessee
articles.summary: Texas just moved to 4-0, beating Tennessee 20-17 in Knoxville. The offense left much to be desired but the Texas defense is championship caliber.
articles.body:
Texas was able to reel in a narrow win over Tennessee, winning 20-17 in Knoxville . The game was defined by a dominant defensive performance, but a poor display from the Longhorns offense.

A late TD drive from Manning and the offense put Texas in a lead they wouldn't give up. Despite the questions coming out, there are a number of great positives to pull as well.

Here are the five things I think we learned from today's win:

This has been an issue for Texas during the Sarkisian era. It seemed like it was on its way to being fixed after Ohio State, but it's returned. Texas finished the day with 11 penalties for 115 yards, including multiple PIs and a silly unsportsmanlike conduct on Colin Simmons. Texas left multiple chances on the table in the first half because they continued to make self-inflicted errors. That needs to be reeled in the rest of the way or Texas will fall short of goals.

PHOTOS: Texas battles Tennessee in SEC opener

This was the worst performance from the offensive line thus far. The Tennessee defense finished with 6 sacks, 10 TFLs and allowed just 1.7 yards per rush. There were a number of communication issues that put Manning under immediate pressure. Considering the strong play early, I'd say it's fair to assume it will get stronger as they get more reps together. However, it has to be fixed against Oklahoma or that could turn into a loss quickly.

There is no question about this now. This defense is going to keep you in every single game because of how good they are. The defense finished with 10 sacks, with Colin Simmons reeling in 5 of them himself. They gave up just 70 yards on 44 carries(1.6 yards/carry). On the backend, the DBs had a few PIs that needed to be fixed but the coverage was overall very strong. Will Muschamp has a championship group that can win Texas multiple games.

Mental toughness is much higher than last season

This is a big takeaway for me. When Tennessee had the punt return to tie the game at 10, the Texas offense immediately made a big play to set up points. Then, early in the 4th quarter, Manning leads an 8 play, 60 yard TD drive, running the ball very well. Finally, when Tennessee scores and recovers the onside kick, your defense finds a way to get one last stop. It's a game that could've gotten away from them multiple times but the mental toughness and focus pulled the Longhorns through.

Texas is set up incredibly well for the rest of the season

Before the season started, it was said an undefeated September would do wonders for Texas. They've done that. This wasn't the prettiest way to get there, but you have two wins over Top 15 teams and a 4-0 record. The rest of the way, you have to face six currently ranked teams in eight games. Having as much wiggle room as possible is massive for this team.

articles.title: How Did Chivas’ Youth Teams Fare Against Querétaro?
articles.summary: The Cantera Rojiblanca was in action this Saturday at Verde Valle, where Guadalajara’s Sub 19 and Sub 21 teams faced Querétaro in matches corresponding to Jo...
articles.body:
The Cantera Rojiblanca was in action this Saturday at Verde Valle, where Guadalajara's Sub 19 and Sub 21 teams faced Querétaro in matches corresponding to Jornada 10 of the Apertura 2026.

The Rebaño finished the day with one win and one loss, as the Sub 19 defeated the Gallos Blancos 2-1, while the Sub 21 fell 4-2.

Keep reading, Chivahermanos, as we take a look at all the details from Guadalajara's youth teams' matches against Querétaro.

Three points for the Rebaño! Guadalajara's Sub 19 defeated Querétaro 2-1 at Verde Valle in their Apertura 2026 Jornada 10 matchup.

The Gallos Blancos took the lead in the 12th minute through Omar Martínez, but Alberto Ascencio's side maintained their intensity and managed to respond, turning the game around to secure the victory at home.

Joseph González stepped up in the 75th minute to level the score and give the Rebaño renewed momentum. Eight minutes later, captain Edgar Vargas found the back of the net in the 83rd minute to complete the comeback and give Chivas all three points at Verde Valle.

With this result, Guadalajara added three points in their Jornada 10 matchup and reached 18 points, placing them fifth in the standings.

Meanwhile, Guadalajara's Sub 21 was unable to earn points against the Gallos Blancos, falling 4-2 to Querétaro at Verde Valle.

The match got off to a lively start, as Bless Ege gave the visitors the lead in the 16th minute, although the Rebaño responded just one minute later with a goal from Aarón Correa. Querétaro regained the lead in the 36th minute through Claudio Robles and extended their advantage in the 42nd minute, once again through Ege.

In the second half, Anwar Ben Rhouma brought Guadalajara within one in the 46th minute, but Bless Ege completed his hat-trick in the 68th minute to make it 4-2.

With this result, Guadalajara remains on 15 points in the Apertura 2026.

articles.title: Wakefield Trinity hailed after stunning win over Wigan Warriors to reach Super League Grand Final: 'No team would have competed with them'
articles.summary: Wakefield Trinity booked their spot in their first-ever Super League Grand Final with a 33-6 win against Wigan Warriors; the victory will see them face Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final; watch the Super League Grand Final live on Sky Sports Main Event on Saturday
articles.body:
A flurry of second-half tries saw Trinity end Wigan's 16-match winning streak , with the visitors leaving Matt Peet's side stunned by their ferocious pace and power.

Wigan went down to 12 men after 45 minutes, with Adam Keighran being sin-binned for a tip-tackle. Wakefield ruthlessly took advantage, scoring three tries while the Australian five-eighth was off the field.

Wigan did impress in the opening exchanges, matching Wakefield for intensity, with Brad O'Neill breaking the deadlock after a tense first 15 minutes.

But the League Leaders' Shield winners, who had two weeks off coming into this match, stumbled in the second half.

"Wigan were bad, but that was completely induced by what Wakefield threw at them," Wilkin told Sky Sports .

"It was a clinical performance that was full of power, pace, energy, enthusiasm and execution.

"Nobody would have competed with Wakefield today. Not one team in Super League.

"I'd go as far as to say some of the great teams we've had in the history of Super League wouldn't have competed with that 80 minutes that Wakefield have dished up."

After Keighran was sent to the bin, Tom Johnston touched down in the corner with a diving finish, before Jack Sinfield beat Junior Nsemba from close range to score another.

They had a third in seven minutes, with Corey Hall sprinting down the wing before smashing his way over the tryline.

Ky Rodwell wrapped up the 27-point win, thanks to some great hands from Jake Trueman.

After the match, Peet lauded Wakefield, adding his Wigan side were "well prepared" but came up second on the night.

"Wakefield were outstandingly good," the Warriors coach said. "All the credit in the world to them, to Daryl. We were outplayed, outcoached, and beaten all ends up.

"Credit to them, it hurts, but the night belongs to them."

A new name on the Super League trophy is now guaranteed, with Trinity to face Warrington Wolves in the Grand Final at Old Trafford next Saturday, which is live on Sky Sports .

Powell left his role with Castleford Tigers at the conclusion of the 2021 Super League season, having guided the side to a Challenge Cup final appearance and their maiden Super League Grand Final.

He was appointed head coach at Wakefield in October 2023, and has been instrumental in lifting the club from the Championship to its first Super League Grand Final, after one of their best seasons on record.

"I think the jury was still out after his spell at Castleford," Wilkin said.

"But there is no doubt that Daryl Powell is an exceptional coach, who can get a group of men organised and directed to success.

"That's what he's done, and he's done it with such style and class.

"Wakefield play with risk and they play the game in a beautiful way."

Ellis: I didn't think in my wildest dreams we'd do that

Wakefield owner Matt Ellis heaped praise on his team following the match:

"It's still not sunk in yet. Four-and-a-half thousand fans still singing away. What a performance.

"That was the best performance in my time owning the club. So proud of them. We just nailed it today, didn't we?

"I didn't think in my wildest dreams [we'd be four scores up].

"I had a good feeling all week about it; all the pressure was on them. We came here, we were confident.

"It's a happy group, but it's an even happier group right now.

"There's so many good stories, three years after relegation, and now we're there!"

articles.title: Michigan State can't keep up with Nebraska in Big Ten opener
articles.summary: Michigan State opened Big Ten play with a 31-13 setback at home.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING — Michigan State was looking to start off Big Ten play on the right foot.

Instead, the Spartans were left in the dust as Nebraska pulled away for a 31-13 win at Spartan Stadium on Saturday, Sept. 26.

Michigan State (2-2, 0-1) grabbed an early lead but it didn't last. Nebraska took a 24-10 lead into halftime and made it a three-score game in the fourth quarter to put it out of reach.
